argument_summary: The admissible record does not support a clean claim that rollout controls alone satisfy policy. It does support a narrower certification posture: aggregate readiness passed by 2.3 percentage points, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the launch starts at 9% with rollback and monitoring. Those facts make certification operationally supportable only if the packet is framed as caveated compliance and explicitly records that the cybersecurity alert triage use case remains below target, remains exposed in the initial cohort, and is therefore still subject to disclosure obligations.
claims_about_business_cost: A no-escalation path is still available if the auditor treats this as caveated compliance rather than clean compliance, because that preserves the locked certification path while accurately documenting the unresolved limitation instead of reopening the decision on unsupported grounds.
claims_about_policy: The policy is not satisfied by reversible rollout or monitoring alone when the affected named use case remains exposed. The strongest supportable reading is that aggregate readiness and deployment controls are relevant supporting controls, while the unresolved requirement is disclosure of the material limitation because there is no approved risk acceptance covering this exposure and no evidence that the rollout excludes the affected segment. Public model-card and risk-monitoring guidance strengthens the case for documented, monitored deployment, but it does not displace the stated internal policy condition.
concessions: The exposed cybersecurity alert triage segment remains below target on lateral-movement alert summarization.
The initial 9% rollout does not exclude that affected segment.
The available risk acceptance draft is not approved and does not address this exposure.
The current record does not support a clean compliant certification based on rollout controls alone.
